title: The Tudors
intro: From Bosworth to the Armada: kings, queens and big changes in Tudor England.

questions.prompt: Who was the first Tudor king?
questions.explanation: Henry VII became the first Tudor king after the Battle of Bosworth.

questions.prompt: At which battle did Henry Tudor defeat Richard III?
questions.explanation: Henry Tudor defeated Richard III at the Battle of Bosworth and became King Henry VII.

questions.prompt: In which year was the Battle of Bosworth?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Bosworth was fought in 1485 and is often seen as the start of the Tudor period.

questions.prompt: Who was Henry VIII's first wife?
questions.explanation: Henry VIII's first wife was Catherine of Aragon, a Spanish princess.

questions.prompt: Henry VIII broke away from the authority of which church leader to create the Church of England?
questions.explanation: Henry VIII broke with the Pope in Rome and made himself head of the Church of England.

questions.prompt: Who was the last Tudor monarch?
questions.explanation: Elizabeth I was the last Tudor monarch. When she died in 1603, James VI of Scotland became king of England.

questions.prompt: What was the large Spanish fleet that tried to invade England in 1588 called?
questions.explanation: The Spanish Armada was defeated in 1588, during the reign of Elizabeth I.

questions.prompt: Edward VI was the son of Henry VIII.
questions.explanation: Edward VI was the son of Henry VIII and Jane Seymour. He became king at the age of nine.

questions.prompt: Which English sailor travelled all the way around the world between 1577 and 1580?
questions.explanation: Francis Drake sailed around the world in his ship, the Golden Hind, during Elizabeth I's reign.

questions.prompt: Elizabeth I never married.
questions.explanation: Elizabeth I never married and had no children, which is why the Tudor line ended with her.

questions.prompt: What name is given to the long struggle for the throne between the royal houses of Lancaster and York in the 1400s?
questions.explanation: The two families had rose badges, red for Lancaster and white for York. Henry VII later combined them in the Tudor rose.

questions.prompt: Which of Henry VIII's wives was the mother of Edward VI?
questions.explanation: Jane Seymour gave birth to Edward in 1537. He was the son Henry had long hoped for.

questions.prompt: Which of Henry VIII's wives outlived him?
questions.explanation: Catherine Parr was Henry's sixth wife. Henry died in 1547 and she lived until the following year.

questions.prompt: Which minister helped Henry VIII close England's monasteries in the 1530s?
questions.explanation: Thomas Cromwell organised the closures. The monasteries' land and riches went to the Crown.

questions.prompt: What is the closing of England's religious houses between 1536 and 1541 known as?
questions.explanation: Over about five years, hundreds of monasteries, abbeys and priories were shut down and their wealth taken by the king.

questions.prompt: What was the 1536 rising in the north of England against Henry VIII's religious changes called?
questions.explanation: Thousands of people in the north marched in protest at the closing of the monasteries and other changes.

questions.prompt: Who is often called the 'Nine Days' Queen' after her very short reign in 1553?
questions.explanation: When Edward VI died, Lady Jane Grey was declared queen, but Mary I won wide support and took the throne within days.

questions.prompt: Mary I tried to bring back which form of Christianity in England?
questions.explanation: Mary I was a devout Catholic and restored the Pope's authority over the English Church during her reign.

questions.prompt: Which of Henry VIII's warships sank in 1545 and was raised from the seabed in 1982?
questions.explanation: The Mary Rose sank in the Solent. Raised in 1982, she and thousands of objects from on board now tell us about Tudor life at sea.

questions.prompt: What was the name of Francis Drake's ship on his voyage around the world?
questions.explanation: Drake set out in a ship called the Pelican and renamed it the Golden Hind during the voyage.

questions.prompt: Henry VII was born at Pembroke Castle. In which country is it?
questions.explanation: The Tudor family had Welsh roots, and Henry landed in Wales in 1485 before marching to Bosworth.

questions.prompt: Which Elizabethan courtier organised expeditions to set up an English colony at Roanoke in North America?
questions.explanation: Raleigh sponsored voyages in the 1580s, and named the area Virginia after Elizabeth I, the 'Virgin Queen'.

questions.prompt: Who became king of England when Elizabeth I died, ending the Tudor era?
questions.explanation: James VI of Scotland became James I of England in 1603, the first Stuart king of England.

questions.prompt: Cardinal Thomas Wolsey lost Henry VIII's favour after failing to get the Pope to agree to what?

options.label: Ending Henry's marriage to Catherine of Aragon
The building of a new navy

questions.explanation: Henry wanted his first marriage cancelled so he could marry Anne Boleyn. When Wolsey could not achieve this, he fell from power.

questions.prompt: Under Edward VI, the Book of Common Prayer meant church services were held in which language?
questions.explanation: Before this, services were in Latin. The 1549 Prayer Book let ordinary people understand the words of worship.

questions.prompt: Mary I was the daughter of Henry VIII and Catherine of Aragon.
questions.explanation: Mary was born in 1516, the only child of Henry and Catherine to survive into adulthood.

questions.prompt: Henry VII was the father of Henry VIII.
questions.explanation: Henry VIII was Henry VII's second son. He became heir after his older brother Arthur died.

questions.prompt: The Spanish Armada successfully landed an army in England in 1588.
questions.explanation: The Armada never landed. English fire ships broke up its formation and storms scattered the fleet as it sailed home.

questions.prompt: In which year did Elizabeth I become queen?
questions.explanation: Elizabeth became queen in 1558 when her half-sister Mary I died.

questions.prompt: In which year did Elizabeth I die, bringing the Tudor period to an end?
questions.explanation: Elizabeth died in 1603 after reigning for over 44 years, and the crown passed to the Stuarts.
